Generate diagnostics table for persephone objects (internal)

Source: R/diagnosticsTable.R
generate_diagnostics_table.Rd

Generate diagnostics table for persephone objects (internal)

Usage

generate_diagnostics_table(x)

Arguments

x

an object of class persephone

Value

A data.frame with one row containing diagnostic measures

Details

The function classifies various diagnostic statistics into quality categories:

  • Normality/Independence tests: "Good" (p ≥ 0.1), "Uncertain" (0.01 ≤ p < 0.1), "Bad" (0.001 ≤ p < 0.01), "Severe" (p < 0.001)

  • Seasonality/TD tests: "Good" (p ≥ 0.1), "Uncertain" (0.05 ≤ p < 0.1), "Bad" (0.01 ≤ p < 0.05), "Severe" (p < 0.01)

  • TD regression F-test (TD_status): small p indicates a significant trading day effect and thus justified trading-day regressors, i.e. the reverse direction of the residual tests: "Good" (p < 0.05), "Uncertain" (0.05 ≤ p < 0.1), "Bad" (p ≥ 0.1)

  • Outliers: "Good" (< 3\

Returned Columns

run

Logical indicating if the model has been run

method

Seasonal adjustment method used (x13 or tramoseats)

type

Type of series ("single" or "aggregate")

seasonality

Result of combined seasonality test

normality

Classification of Doornik-Hansen normality test

independence

Classification of Ljung-Box test for independence

QS_seas

Classification of QS test for residual seasonality

F_seas

Classification of F-test for residual seasonality

combSA_all

Combined test for calendar effects in SA (all observations)

combSA_last

Combined test for calendar effects in SA (last year)

combI_all

Combined test for calendar effects in irregular (all observations)

combI_last

Combined test for calendar effects in irregular (last year)

fTestSA_td

F-test for trading day effects in SA series

TD_Ftest

P-value of regression F-test for trading days. NA if the final model contains no trading-day regressors — e.g. templates without calendar effects ("rsa3") or when the automatic pre-test (td.test = "Remove", as in "rsa5c") dropped them; use td.test = "None" to force their inclusion

TD_status

Classification of the regression F-test for trading days: "Good" if the trading day effect is significant (small p), "Bad" if the trading-day regressors are not justified by the data

logTransform

Logical indicating if log transformation was applied

arimaMdl

ARIMA model specification as string

nOutliers_Q

Classification of outlier proportion

nOutliers

Number of outliers in the model

nAutoout

Number of automatically detected outliers (see the autoout column of getOutliers)

nRecentout

Number of outliers falling into the last observations of the series (see the recentout column of getOutliers)

nSigRecentout

Number of significant recent outliers: those recent outliers whose absolute t-statistic exceeds the model's critical value, i.e. recentout and abs(t) > crit.value in getOutliers. This is the same threshold JDemetra+ uses to decide whether an effect enters the model at all, so automatically detected recent outliers essentially always count. The value differs from nRecentout mainly for manually specified recent outliers that do not reach the threshold, and for outliers with a non-estimable t-statistic (e.g. coef.type = "FIXED"), which are never counted as significant.

Q

Composite quality indicator built from the X-11 M-statistics (M1 to M11): a weighted mean of the individual statistics, each of which ranges from 0 to 3 and is accepted below 1; a value below 1 indicates a satisfactory quality

Q2

The same composite computed without the M2 statistic (Q-M2)

nMstatOutside

Number of X-11 M-statistics outside their acceptance limits (value above 1); statistics that could not be computed do not count, and the value is NA when no M-statistics are available at all (e.g. TRAMO-SEATS)

TotalQ

Overall quality summary (JDemetra+ node quality.summary): an aggregate of all standard diagnostic tests (residual, forecasting, outlier, spectral, seasonality and trading-day tests, plus the M-statistics Q/Q2 for X-13 or the Wiener-Kolmogorov tests for SEATS), classified as Good, Uncertain, Bad, Severe or Undefined. See the diagnostics vignette for details
